prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters, simple rounded people with big round eyes, small dot pupils and overbites, flat colour and black outlines everywhere except the faces, which are rendered with startling real skin: pores, stubble, sweat, tired wet eyes. Every flat colour is laid on with thick visible oil brushstrokes. Only the bodies, clothes and places are cartoon: every face in the frame, however small, is painted as real human skin with wrinkles, pores, bags under the eyes and real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, and no feature is exaggerated. Over the shoulder of a landlord at the top of a narrow 1930s tenement stairwell: his fur coat collar and plump open palm, heavy with gold rings, fill the near foreground, held out and waiting. Below him, climbing the steep worn stairs towards the palm, a heavy-set clean-shaven Black baker in his fifties with a shaved head, a broken nose and a round double chin, in a floury sweat-stained vest, a thin brown paper pay packet in his hand, his face tilted up, exhausted. Peeling green paint, a cracked banister, one bare bulb hanging above the landlord throwing hard light down the stairs. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
